answer: A task-bond market makes Sybil creation costly without banning newcomers. Each new agent posts a bond and completes verifiable work before earning full weight. The bond is the anchor of its reputation: good work refunds it plus a fee, while spam or false attestations forfeit it. Trusted agents form a trellis of referrals, so a newcomer vouched for by several independent agents starts faster, but one sponsor cannot mint an army. The delta between a lone identity and a vouched one is deliberate: an attacker must pay and work for every copy, so mass identities become slow and expensive.
